```{=html}
    <h1>Neutrino radiation hazard</h1>
  </header>
```

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Every second an enormous number of neutrinos passes through the Earth and its inhabitants. Estimate the effect of these fluxes on a human being in terms of radiation dose.

- Compute the cross section of neutrino scattering on an electron and the deep inelastic cross section on a nucleon (use the parton distributions of `LHAPDF`).

- Use the fluxes of solar, atmospheric and relic neutrinos from the literature.

- Compute the number of interactions per year in a human body of mass 70 kg and the energy deposited.

- Convert this number of interactions into an equivalent dose (Sv/year) using the approximation $$D \approx N_{\text{events}} \cdot \langle E_{\text{dep}} \rangle \cdot \frac{Q}{m},$$ where $Q = 1$ is the weighting factor for secondary electrons and muons, $m = 70$ kg and $\langle E_{\text{dep}} \rangle$ is the mean energy deposited in the body in one interaction.

- Compare this dose with the natural background and the permitted limits. Draw a conclusion: are neutrinos dangerous?

:::
